key_insight: The paper builds a fully algebraic multiscale coarse space for two-level overlapping Schwarz preconditioners by using reduced boundary-condition interface problems and energy-minimizing extensions, making the coarse correction robust to strong heterogeneity.
engineering_relevance: This gives a matrix-based preconditioner that can improve scalability for heterogeneous diffusion and elasticity problems without requiring explicit multiscale finite-element mesh construction.
method: Construct the coarse space from the system matrix alone via an algebraic MsFEM formulation.
Solve reduced boundary condition problems on interface slabs, then extend them by energy minimization.
Embed the framework in an energy-minimizing form so it also applies to linear elasticity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that, for high-contrast inclusions on coarse nodes, iteration counts and condition numbers stay unchanged as contrast increases, and in 3D log-normal diffusion the method matches GDSW iteration counts with a coarse problem about 10× smaller.
watch_item: Performance depends on how well the interface-based slabs and coarse-node selection capture rigid-body and heterogeneity effects, especially for elasticity and unstructured decompositions.
paper_title: An algebraic multiscale framework for two-level overlapping Schwarz preconditioners
